stem:
Firoz hears that this week's reading target is $140\%$ of last week's base of $50$ pages.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: 140% means the same as the base of 50 pages, because any percent names the base.
The base of 50 pages is produced by this week's target, so start from this week and ignore the percent.
140% of 50 is $1.4\times50=70$ pages, which is more than the base.
140% of 50 is 40 pages, reading only the digits above 100.

teacher.key_rationale: A percentage above 100 means the quantity exceeds the named base: 140% of 50 is 70 pages. Treating 140% as equal to the base drops that meaning. Reversing so the base comes from this week's count flips the relation. Reading only the excess digits as 40 is outside the percent-of-base hinge.
